title: Coefficient compositor pasting through replacement and model isomorphisms
statement:
Let $\mathcal C_{i,R}$, for $i=0,1,2$ and $R=A,B$, be categories [def-nagata-category]. A functor preserves identities and composition; a natural transformation $u:F\to G$ has components with $G(a)u_x=u_yF(a)$, and a natural isomorphism has invertible components. Composition below is right to left. Specify functors $T_i:\mathcal C_{i,A}\to\mathcal C_{i,B}$ and, for each $R$, functors $F_R,E_R:\mathcal C_{0,R}\to\mathcal C_{1,R}$, $P_R:\mathcal C_{1,R}\to\mathcal C_{2,R}$, $Q_R:\mathcal C_{0,R}\to\mathcal C_{2,R}$, natural isomorphisms $c_R:F_R\simeq E_R$, $\alpha_R:P_RF_R\simeq Q_R$, and natural transformations
$$\beta_F:T_1F_A\to F_BT_0,\quad\beta_P:T_2P_A\to P_BT_1,\quad\beta_Q:T_2Q_A\to Q_BT_0,\quad\sigma:T_1E_A\to E_BT_0.$$
Assume the following equalities of natural transformations:
$$c_BT_0\circ\beta_F=\sigma\circ T_1c_A,\qquad \beta_Q\circ T_2\alpha_A=\alpha_BT_0\circ P_B\beta_F\circ\beta_PF_A.$$
For $\lambda_R=\alpha_R\circ P_R(c_R^{-1})$, one has
$$\beta_F\circ T_1(c_A^{-1})=c_B^{-1}T_0\circ\sigma,\qquad \beta_Q\circ T_2\lambda_A=\lambda_BT_0\circ P_B\sigma\circ\beta_PE_A.$$
The equalities are natural in the input; invertibility of the $\beta$ transformations is not assumed.
For a second such system on the same categories and with the same $T_i,E_R,\sigma$, let $\rho_{F,R}:F_R\simeq F'_R$, $\rho_{P,R}:P_R\simeq P'_R$, $\rho_{Q,R}:Q_R\simeq Q'_R$ satisfy
$$c'_R\rho_{F,R}=c_R,\qquad \alpha'_R\circ P'_R(\rho_{F,R})\circ(\rho_{P,R}F_R)=\rho_{Q,R}\circ\alpha_R,$$
and, for $X=F,P,Q$ with source/target indices $(i,j)=(0,1),(1,2),(0,2)$ respectively,
$$\beta'_X\circ T_j\rho_{X,A}=\rho_{X,B}T_i\circ\beta_X.$$
Then
$$\lambda'_R\circ(\rho_{P,R}E_R)=\rho_{Q,R}\circ\lambda_R.$$
Under these source and target identifications the displayed $\lambda$ coefficient equation for the primed system is the one for the unprimed system. In particular changing only $F_R$ cancels its comparison completely. These conclusions respect identities and composites of model isomorphisms. No additive, exactness, tensor-flatness or nonemptiness hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Work componentwise and retain right-to-left composition. The category laws of [def-nagata-category] allow reassociation and deletion of identity factors. In particular, cancellation of an invertible factor means composing with its specified inverse, not cancelling any coefficient map. A functor $H$ carries an inverse pair $ab=1$, $ba=1$ to the inverse pair $H(a)H(b)=1$, $H(b)H(a)=1$. These observations apply to every occurrence of $c_R$, $\rho_{X,R}$ and their functor images below.

proof.text: Postcompose $c_BT_0\circ\beta_F=\sigma\circ T_1c_A$ with $c_B^{-1}T_0$ and precompose with $T_1(c_A^{-1})$. The left side becomes $\beta_F\circ T_1(c_A^{-1})$, while the right side becomes $(c_B^{-1}T_0)\circ\sigma\circ T_1(c_A)\circ T_1(c_A^{-1})=(c_B^{-1}T_0)\circ\sigma$. This proves the first required equation using only the assumed square and inverse identities.

source.place: Charts, coefficient compatibility for the specified left identification; old scalar-normalization Steps 3 and 4 and the coefficient/refinement calculations of Step 5

proof.text:
At $x\in\mathcal C_{0,A}$ apply the defining naturality of $\beta_P$ to $c_{A,x}^{-1}:E_Ax\to F_Ax$:
$$\beta_{P,F_Ax}\,T_2P_A(c_{A,x}^{-1})=P_BT_1(c_{A,x}^{-1})\,\beta_{P,E_Ax}.$$
Suppress $x$ in the remaining factors. Substituting the assumed compositor square, this identity, and Step 2 gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\beta_QT_2\lambda_A
&=\alpha_BT_0\,P_B\beta_F\,\beta_PF_A\,T_2P_A(c_A^{-1})\\
&=\alpha_BT_0\,P_B(\beta_F\,T_1(c_A^{-1}))\,\beta_PE_A\\
&=\alpha_BT_0\,P_B(c_B^{-1}T_0)\,P_B\sigma\,\beta_PE_A\\
&=\lambda_BT_0\,P_B\sigma\,\beta_PE_A.
\end{aligned}$$
Each rewriting is functoriality or one of the displayed equations; no inverse of $\beta_P$ or $\beta_F$ occurs.

source.place: Charts, coefficient compatibility for the specified left identification; old scalar-normalization Steps 3 and 4 and the coefficient/refinement calculations of Step 5

proof.text:
For one ring $R$, suppress $R$ and put $r=\rho_F$, $s=\rho_P$, $t=\rho_Q$. The hypothesis $c'r=c$ implies $c'^{-1}=rc^{-1}$ by multiplication with inverses. Naturality of $s:P\to P'$ at $c_x^{-1}$ says $P'(c_x^{-1})s_{E x}=s_{F x}P(c_x^{-1})$. Consequently
$$\begin{aligned}
\lambda'\,(sE)&=\alpha' P'(c'^{-1})(sE)\\
&=\alpha' P'r\,P'(c^{-1})(sE)\\
&=\alpha' P'r\,(sF)P(c^{-1})\\
&=t\alpha P(c^{-1})=t\lambda.
\end{aligned}$$
The penultimate equality is exactly the assumed $\alpha$ model square. This proves the model formula for both $A$ and $B$. If only $F$ changes then $s$ and $t$ are identities, and the formula reads $\lambda'=\lambda$.

source.place: Charts, coefficient compatibility for the specified left identification; old scalar-normalization Steps 3 and 4 and the coefficient/refinement calculations of Step 5

proof.text:
Write $s_R=\rho_{P,R}$ and $t_R=\rho_{Q,R}$. Let $L=\beta_Q T_2\lambda_A$ and $L'=\beta'_Q T_2\lambda'_A$ be the two left sides of the coefficient equation. Precompose $L'$ with the source identification $T_2(s_AE_A)$. By Step 4 and the assumed $Q$ coefficient model square,
$$L'\,T_2(s_AE_A)=\beta'_Q T_2(t_A\lambda_A)=(t_BT_0)\,\beta_Q T_2\lambda_A=(t_BT_0)L.$$
Thus the left sides agree after exactly the specified endpoint identifications.

source.place: Charts, coefficient compatibility for the specified left identification; old scalar-normalization Steps 3 and 4 and the coefficient/refinement calculations of Step 5

proof.text:
Put $H=\lambda_BT_0\,P_B\sigma\,\beta_PE_A$ and $H'=\lambda'_BT_0\,P'_B\sigma\,\beta'_PE_A$. At $x$, the $P$ coefficient model square gives $\beta'_{P,E_Ax}T_2(s_{A,E_Ax})=s_{B,T_1E_Ax}\beta_{P,E_Ax}$. Naturality of $s_B$ at $\sigma_x:T_1E_Ax\to E_BT_0x$ then gives $P'_B(\sigma_x)s_{B,T_1E_Ax}=s_{B,E_BT_0x}P_B(\sigma_x)$. With Step 4 these yield
$$\begin{aligned}
H' T_2(s_AE_A)&=\lambda'_BT_0\,P'_B\sigma\,(s_BT_1E_A)\,\beta_PE_A\\
&=\lambda'_BT_0\,(s_BE_BT_0)\,P_B\sigma\,\beta_PE_A\\
&=(t_BT_0)H.
\end{aligned}$$
Together with Step 5 this identifies the two equations: $L'=H'$ if and only if $L=H$, because $T_2(s_AE_A)$ and $t_BT_0$ have inverses by Step 1. In particular Step 3 proves the primed equation under these identifications.

source.place: Charts, coefficient compatibility for the specified left identification; old scalar-normalization Steps 3 and 4 and the coefficient/refinement calculations of Step 5

proof.text:
Check identities and composites explicitly. For two successive model changes write $(r,s,t)$ and $(r',s',t')$, suppressing $R$. Identity changes delete identity factors in Steps 4--6. For composites, $c''r'r=c'r=c$ and, by naturality of $s'$ at $r$,
$$\begin{aligned}
\alpha''P''(r'r)((s's)F)
&=\alpha''P''r'\,P''r\,(s'F)(sF)\\
&=\alpha''P''r'\,(s'F')P'r\,(sF)\\
&=t'\alpha'P'r\,(sF)=t't\alpha.
\end{aligned}$$
For each $X$, its successive coefficient squares give
$$\beta''_X T_j(\rho'_{X,A}\rho_{X,A})=(\rho'_{X,B}T_i)\beta'_X T_j\rho_{X,A}=((\rho'_{X,B}\rho_{X,B})T_i)\beta_X.$$
The composite is therefore another allowed model change. Moreover $\lambda''(s's)E=t'\lambda'(sE)=t't\lambda$. The endpoint identifications in Steps 5--6 compose to $T_2((s'_As_A)E_A)$ and $(t'_Bt_B)T_0$, since functors preserve composition. This proves the claimed coherence without making any choice of comparisons.

source.place: Charts, coefficient compatibility for the specified left identification; old scalar-normalization Steps 3 and 4 and the coefficient/refinement calculations of Step 5

proof.text:
Finally all formulas are natural in the input. This is checked from the definition in the statement: for $u:F\to G$, $v:G\to H$ and $a:x\to y$,
$$H(a)v_xu_x=v_yG(a)u_x=v_yu_yF(a).$$
Postwhiskering this equality by a functor preserves it by functoriality; prewhiskering replaces $a$ by its functor image. Naturality of an inverse follows by multiplying $E(a)c_x=c_yF(a)$ with $c_y^{-1}$ and $c_x^{-1}$, giving $F(a)c_x^{-1}=c_y^{-1}E(a)$. Thus every composite and whiskering used above, including $\lambda$, is a natural transformation, and the component equalities are equalities of natural transformations. If an input category is empty the same statements are vacuous component equalities. Only the category laws, the inline definitions, and the stated hypotheses were used, so no extra additive, exactness, flatness, or nonemptiness assumption enters.
